findings.issue: Write path decodes arbitrary-length Base64 with no max bound (Android Base64.decode / iOS Data(base64Encoded:) / Electron N-API Buffer). A single huge write from JS (or Electron IPC if general BLE write is ever exposed) can allocate multi-MB buffers and stress GATT/main. ATT payloads are tens–hundreds of bytes; long-write already chunks at app layer.
findings.proposed_fix: Reject valueBase64 / byte arrays above a sane cap (e.g. 512KiB) with CharacteristicInvalidDataFormat before decode/radio; document that software long-write is the path for large transfers. Apply same cap in encoding.base64ToBytes optional maxLength for host edges.
